Read tests/unit/test_eval_compare.py:129-141 (six parametrized cases, dialect="mysql") and src/sqllens/eval/compare.py:39-84. The repo logic is as claimed. normalize_sql parses every statement with sqlglot.parse(read=mysql), drops None entries, raises ParseError if none remain, and joins the rendered statements with '; '. compare_sql returns PASS or CHANGED on equality of the normalized strings. It wraps SqlglotError as SqlComparisonError, and compare maps that to ERROR. So, assuming sqlglot behaves as expected, the six cases give: a differing second statement is CHANGED, whitespace/casing/trailing-';' differences are PASS, an extra statement is CHANGED, a 'SELECT (' side is ERROR, and an empty string is ERROR. However, three of these outcomes depend on sqlglot's runtime behavior. 'SELECT (' must raise a SqlglotError. A trailing ';' must not yield an extra statement. sqlglot.parse('') must yield no non-None statement. No dependency_sources were supplied, the view inventory has no sqlglot source, and no committed vendor copy exists, so I could not read sqlglot's parser or tokenizer. I also did not run the test.
